item.title: Draymond Green reveals what Yaxel Lendeborg was trying to do after Kevin Durant signed his jersey
item.description: Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images Yaxel Lendeborg had a dream-come-true moment recently thanks to Kevin Durant. The rookie faced the NBA icon during the Golden State Warriors’ recent defeat to the Houston Rockets, and they went toe-to-toe on the court. Durant was impressed by what he saw from Lendeborg, so much so that he asked for a jersey swap after the game. What happened next will put a smile on your face. Yaxel Lendeborg wanted to leave the arena wearing Kevin Durant’s signed shirt Durant is one of the best players we’ve ever seen in the NBA. The 38-year-old has been a role model for many young players growing up, including Lendeborg, who has revealed that he always played as KD in the NBA 2K video game series. After the game, despite the defeat, Green has revealed that the rookie was like a little kid waiting for Durant to swap shirts, get it signed and take a picture with him. Once that happened, Lendeborg apparently tried to leave the arena wearing KD’s shirt, which made Green realise that he is still a kid, even though he has been tearing it up in the league this season. He said in his YouTube video : “It was d*** to see KD and Yax have their moment last night. They went at it a little bit in the game, but then after the game, KD mentioned to Yax that he wanted his jersey. “Yax was happy as hell. He wanted KD’s jersey. KD signed the jersey for him, and Yax was trying to wear the jersey out of the arena. “That’s when you get to see like Yax is still really a** big kid, and it’s moments like that where you get to see like: ‘Yo, this rookie is killing everybody, but he’s still really a big a** kid and maturing and coming into his own.’ He was happy as hell to have that moment with KD. Green also revealed that even before the game was over, he saw Lendeborg talking about swapping jerseys with Durant, getting it signed and taking a picture with him. If it was anyone else, Green says he wouldn’t have allowed it because the Golden State Warriors lost, but because it was a legend like Durant, he let it go. The veteran concluded by saying: “That was a super d*** moment to see, and happy Yax got to have that moment. “One thing about KD, KD ain’t just giving you no respect on the basketball court. To go and gain that respect is big time, and it says a lot about Yax.” Read more: ‘Kerr won’t like this’ – Warriors fans concerned about what Yaxel Lendeborg just said ‘This kid’: Draymond Green says he just cannot allow Yaxel Lendeborg to do one thing during Warriors games ‘He’s skinnier than me’: Yaxel Lendeborg makes brutal admission after facing Victor Wembanyama

item.title: Detroit Lions Announce Roster Move Ahead of Patriots Showdown in Germany
item.description: The Detroit Lions have announced another roster move ahead of Sunday’s highly anticipated matchup against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. With the team’s linebacker depth already being tested by injuries, Detroit is bringing in some additional reinforcements. On Saturday morning, the Lions officially announced that linebacker Owen Pappoe has been elevated from the practice squad to the Active/Inactive list for Sunday’s Week 10 showdown. The move gives Detroit additional depth at linebacker and on special teams as Dan Campbell’s squad looks to extend its winning streak to five games. NFL Arizona Cardinals linebacker Owen Pappoe. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Lions Continue Making Linebacker Adjustments Pappoe, 26, originally joined the Lions’ practice squad on November 4 as part of a series of roster changes designed to strengthen the position. According to the team’s official transaction history , Detroit also added linebackers K.J. Britt and Joe Bachie to its active roster that day. Those moves came amid a difficult stretch for the Lions’ linebacker group, which has been dealing with multiple injuries. Detroit previously placed Jack Campbell on injured reserve following the frightening neck injury he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings. Rookie Jimmy Rolder was also placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury earlier this month. Pappoe brings NFL experience to the group after spending his first three seasons with the Arizona Cardinals. According to his official Lions player profile , the former Auburn standout appeared in 49 games for Arizona, recording 66 combined tackles and five passes defended. Originally selected by Arizona in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL Draft, Pappoe also spent time with the Tennessee Titans before joining Detroit. Lions Preparing for Patriots in Munich Saturday’s elevation comes as the Lions finalize their preparations for Sunday’s international matchup at Allianz Arena. Detroit has already ruled out three players against New England , including safety Kerby Joseph, center Cade Mays, and cornerback D.J. Reed. While Pappoe’s elevation does not guarantee that he will see defensive snaps, it provides the Lions with additional flexibility at linebacker and on special teams. Given the team’s recent injuries, that depth could prove valuable against the Patriots. The Lions enter Sunday’s game with a 6-2 record and four consecutive victories, while New England sits at 5-4. Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX .

item.title: Milwaukee Brewers Rumor on Jake Bauers Replacement Emerges, Including Prospect Who Started 2026 in Single-A
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Unsurprisingly, it is very likely that the Milwaukee Brewers will go with an internal option to replace Jake Bauers at first base next season. And one of those players in contention began last season in Single-A. The years of waiting and suffering finally ended in October. After nearly 60 years in existence, the Brewers can finally call themselves the champions of MLB after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in the 2026 World Series. While several players played huge roles in their championship run, their journeyman first baseman made a major impact. Bauers knocked in career highs in home runs (26) and RBIs (86), and even had a career-best 11 stolen bases during the 2026 regular season. However, he was also very good in the playoffs, including posting six RBIs in the NLCS versus the Los Angeles Dodgers . As expected, Milwaukee Brewers lose Jake Bauers in free agency Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers (9) misses the catch and Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero (13) is safe at first base during the twelfth inning during Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. on Oct 27, 2026. That is why his departure in free agency was expected this month. Well, that eventuality became a reality on Friday when the Boston Red Sox gave the 30-year-old a four-year deal worth $58 million . Bauers’ exit leaves a sizable hole in the batting order for 2027 — if there even is a 2027 MLB season. After banking some big money during their title run, it would make sense if the Brewers reinvested in the team and spent on finding a worthwhile replacement at first. However, that would not be business as usual for the club that is always looking to use their money as efficiently as possible. Brewers to address first base with internal options in 2027 Milwaukee Brewers infield prospect Andrew Fischer hits during spring training workouts Tuesday, February 17, 2026, at American Family Fields of Phoenix in Phoenix, Arizona. According to sources who spoke to The Athletic’s Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal, it is very unlikely the Brewers look outside the organization for a Bauers’ replacement. So who will be manning first base in 2027? The MLB insiders claim they will probably go with a platoon at first base featuring Andrew Vaughn and a stud prospect from their stacked minor league system. Andrew Fischer (No. 5), Blake Burke (No. 12), and Luke Adams (No. 13) were top 15 prospects for Milwaukee to end the season (via MLB.com) . The latter pair both finished the year at AAA and played solid when healthy. However, Sammon and Rosenthal suggest Fischer is a very realistic option to get a big-league spot after starting the 2026 season in Single-A. Especially since he hits lefty and smashed 48 homers across Single-A and Double-A last season. If he looks good in spring training, he could bypass Triple-A and reach MLB at just 22 years old. item.title: Lions owner Sheila Hamp taps keg, predicts 'blue wave' in Munich
item.description: MUNICH, Germany — It was owner Sheila Hamp's turn to tap the keg at the famed Hofbräuhaus beer hall as the celebration of Detroit Lions football continued in Munich, Germany, on Saturday, Nov. 14. With her family in tow and hundreds of Lions fans dying to grab a glimpse, Hamp put a another charge into the week-long party by serving up some hearty helpings of German beer and predicting a “blue wave” at Allianz Arena when the Lions play the New England Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 15. “I think it’s gonna be a blue wave, for sure,” said a beer-dampened Hamp. “I was actually looking for Patriots fans today, just out of curiosity. I think I saw two.” The Lions have proclaimed that they want to be Germany’s team throughout the week, and that might be understating the team’s presence in Munich over the last few days. Wojo: Germany embraces Amon-Ra St. Brown, its favored Lion Fans have packed into Hofbräuhaus, the Lions’ official fan pub, from open to close over the last few days, as appearances from legends Barry Sanders and Calvin Johnson have highlighted the week’s festivities. On Friday and Saturday, throngs of people poured through the team’s fan fest, where the goal has been to bring Detroit to Germany. Hamp said it’s been “absolutely incredible” to see the amount of Lions fans that have shown up in Munich. “They're everywhere in the streets. It's so incredible,” Hamp said. “Our fans are the best.” Sheila’s turn to tap the keg. The vibes are off the charts (and my camera now has beer all over it) pic.twitter.com/V9JHxIZcI6 — Nolan Bianchi (@nolanbianchi) November 14, 2026 Hamp added that the sheer volume of Lions fans is “way more” than she expected. “I saw plane-fulls of people and that kind of thing before I actually got here, but it's more than I ever thought. It's amazing,” Hamp said. Flight stop fallout: Some Lions fans dodge flight delays at DTW, head to Germany for game Of course, this is also a business trip. Hamp said she’s confident that coach Dan Campbell will have the team ready to go when the Lions kick off against New England. “We're ready. It's gonna be great,” she said. “We're gonna take over the stadium.” Predictions: Lions vs. New England Patriots nbianchi@detroitnews.com @nolanbianchi This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Lions owner Sheila Hamp taps keg, predicts 'blue wave' in Munich

item.title: Glendale loses Arizona Fall League semifinal, Eduardo Quintero led Dodgers minors in walks
item.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 15: Eduardo Quintero #16 of the Los Angeles Dodgers adjusts his elbow guard during a game between the Surprise Saguaros and Glendale Desert Dogs at Camelback Ranch on October 15, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Glendale Desert Dogs once again scored late in a playoff game, plating four total runs over the final three innings. But that came after trailing 10-0 in a loss to the Surprise Saguaros. Glendale was eliminated in the Arizona Fall League semifinals. The game started two hours, 15 minutes late due to rain, but that didn’t hamper Surprise from scoring early. The good news for Glendale starter Brooks Auger, a Dodgers right-hander, is that he did not allow a hit in his 1 2/3 innings. But Auger did walk five of his 10 batters faced, three of whom scored. It didn’t help that Surprise stole four bases off Auger, two each in the second and third innings. Auger allowed seven steals in as many attempts in his 13 innings in the Arizona Fall League, with 12 runs allowed. Midwest League runners stole 28 bases in 36 attempts (77.8 percent) against Auger in his 17 starts and 59 2/3 innings for Great Lakes this season. Charles Davalan doubled and scored as the designated hitter in his five at bats. Free passes Eduardo Quintero singled once in his four at-bats, ending his Arizona Fall League with nine hits, including one double, in 58 at-bats. But he also walked once, giving him 23 walks and 20 strikeouts in his 19 AFL games, hitting .155/.405/.172. The walk on Friday followed three walks Tuesday for Quintero in Glendale’s penultimate regular season contest and four walks in Thursday’s playoff win. He finished off his season with eight walks in his final 16 plate appearances. Quintero walked 23 times in his 84 plate appearances (27.4 percent), following a stellar 17.4-percent walk rate during the regular season, all but one game with High-A Great Lakes. He walked 88 times in both 2025 and 2026, with a 16.3-percent walk rate in 2025 between Low-A Rancho Cucamonga and High-A. Counting his two walks in three Midwest League playoff games in High-A and one walk in three Texas League playoff games for Double-A Tulsa, Quintero in his 137 games finished with 114 walks on the season, surpassing James Tibbs III, who walked 113 times in 145 games for Triple-A Oklahoma City between the regular season, Pacific Coast League playoffs, and Triple-A championship game. Friday score Surprise 10, Glendale 4 Glendale’s season is over.

item.title: Roma Could Welcome Dybala and Svilar Back Against Parma
item.description: The Roma players Mile Svilar, Paulo Dybala during the Serie A match Enilive Roma-Fiorentina at the Olympic Stadium. Rome (Italy) May 04th, 2026 (Photo by Massimo Insabato/Archivio Massimo Insabato/Mondadori Portfolio via Getty Images) If you polled fans of any major football club, most would probably agree that the international break rarely comes at a good time. Whether your club is riding a heater and risks losing momentum or coming off a tough result and now has to sit and stew for two weeks, these forced pauses can come at a cost. Roma finds itself caught between those two extremes during this break, riding the high of an 18-match unbeaten streak in Italy while licking the wounds of two high-profile Champions League collapses. Despite that awkward existence, good news is on the horizon, and it involves two of the club’s most important players, Paulo Dybala and Mile Svilar. While his scoring touch has vanished this season, Dybala has seemingly turned back the clock this fall, stringing together a series of performances reminiscent of his Juventus peak. However, despite that fine form, Dybala’s injury history finally caught up with him, as the 32-year-old playmaker has been sidelined for the past month with a calf injury. While Gian Piero Gasperini has adapted well enough, using increasingly heavy doses of Matías Soulé and Rodrigo Mora, Roma is set to welcome Dybala back to the fold. According to Il Messaggero, Dybala is poised to return to action when Roma squares off against Parma next week, but he won’t be the only familiar face returning after an extended absence. Svilar, sidelined for nearly six weeks with a fractured toe, could make his long-awaited return to the pitch next Sunday, ending Pierluigi Gollini’s intermezzo between the sticks. With another busy slate of fixtures coming up between Parma on the 21st and the winter recess on December 19th, Roma will need all hands on deck as they attempt to keep pace with Inter and Lazio at the top of the table, to say nothing of advancing in the Champions League.

item.title: Russell Wilson Addresses NC State Head Coaching Rumors
item.description: Photo by John Nacion/Variety via Getty Images Russell Wilson isn't ruling out a return to college football, but he's not rushing to leave his new job at CBS Sports, either. Days after reports surfaced that the retired NFL quarterback interviewed for the head coaching position at NC State, Wilson addressed the speculation during a Friday, November 6 appearance on Today with Jenna and Sheinelle . And while he acknowledged the significance of hearing from his former school, he made it clear that he's enjoying life on the other side of the camera. "Well, listen, when your alma mater calls, you always answer," Wilson said when asked about the reported interview. "Listen, I love doing what I'm doing." Wilson, who retired from the NFL in June after 14 seasons, has spent the past several months settling into his role as an analyst for CBS Sports. Despite his reported interest in the NC State opening, he isn't making any announcements about abandoning television for the sidelines. "CBS is amazing, it's a blast," he said. "I'm focused on right now, and now is loving what I'm doing on TV." The comments come after ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Wilson interviewed for the Wolfpack's head coaching vacancy on Nov. 3. NC State is searching for a replacement for Dave Doeren, who was fired Oct. 24, and Wilson isn't the only former quarterback with ties to the program under consideration. item.title: Napoli consider Stanislav Lobotka exit due to contract issues
item.description: Napoli consider Stanislav Lobotka exit due to contract issues Serie A side Napoli are facing the possibility of losing several players in the next few months and one of them could be Stanislav Lobotka. Tuttomercatoweb report that the midfielder could be a candidate to depart at the end of the campaign. This is mainly due to considerations regarding his contract, which runs out in the summer of 2027. While Napoli do have the option to renew it for another season, that isn’t certain. In fact, the possibility if far-fetched, mainly because of the Partenopei’s concerns over his high salary and ongoing fitness troubles. A renewal will mean that Lobotka might want higher figures, which Napoli do not want to guarantee. They would much rather sign a replacement, hand him a lower wage and build with a younger squad as the title winner won’t even hand them a capital gain in the future due to his age. Exit will be sensible While Lobotka does well when he plays, he has stopped being too reliable because of his fitness, which has become worse in recent seasons. This should be the biggest concern for Napoli, who have had to make do with without them – as they are now. These issues will keep growing, as the players grows older. Kaustubh Pandey – GIFN

item.title: Big boost for Barcelona as Brazil consider sending star attacker back after red card vs Japan
item.description: Big boost for Barcelona as Brazil consider sending star attacker back after red card vs Japan Raphinha endured one of the most frustrating games of the season so far as Brazil fell to a 3-2 defeat to Japan in a friendly in Singapore. The forward had started the game as a right winger and was taken off in the 71st minute. He then witnessed Brazil concede a late winner, leaving him and Carlo Ancelotti frustrated, as they complained to the referees about a foul in the lead-up to the goal. Both of them were shown a red card for their protest , which effectively leaves Raphinha unavailable for the next friendly against Singapore. Brazil consider sending Raphinha back It was a frustrating evening for Raphinha vs Japan. (Photo by Ashok Kumar/Getty Images) According to Diario SPORT , Brazil is now considering sending Raphinha back after he picked up a red card against Japan. The forward won’t be available for the friendly against Singapore, as FIFA laws for red cards apply to friendlies as well. That means Raphinha won’t be able to play against Singapore, and Ancelotti cannot be on the touchline either. This leaves Raphinha’s presence in the Brazil team practically useless, as the Selecao are only playing two friendly this international break. Return to Barcelona makes most sense Hansi Flick would love to have Raphinha return to Barcelona. (Photo by Ashok Kumar/Getty Images) Raphinha’s early return to Barcelona, therefore, is the most logical outcome for all parties involved. The Brazilian has already asked Ancelotti to manage his game-time due to his injury concerns in the past and the fact that he doesn’t want to pick up an injury at this crucial juncture of the campaign. An early return to Barcelona, to that end, could help him recover from the long travel to Singapore and the forward can continue his preparation at Ciutat Esportiva. Barcelona’s next game is against Villarreal next Sunday, where the Catalans simply cannot afford to lose points, especially with Real Madrid currently on a run of eight consecutive wins in all competitions. Raphinha’s presence in that game could prove to be crucial. So it will be interesting to see whether or not the former Leeds United star will be given the green light to return to Barcelona this week.

item.title: Purpose, Passion, Persistence: The Three Pillars Behind Joshua Pacio’s Reinvention
item.description: For over a decade, ONE Strawweight MMA World Champion Joshua “The Passion” Pacio built his legacy in ONE Championship on blistering hands and razor-sharp reflexes. His most profound transformation, however, took shape strictly on the mats, where a gifted striker willingly started over to become a complete martial artist. The Filipino superstar defends his undisputed crown against Japanese submission specialist Keito “Pocket Monk” Yamakita at ONE SAMURAI 5 this Wednesday, November 18, broadcasting live from EBARA WAVE Arena Ota in Tokyo. And he promises to show his evolution on martial arts’ biggest stage. View this post on Instagram His opponent, Yamakita, brings a smothering ground game and a stellar five-fight winning streak into the World Title clash. Pacio, however, now actively welcomes the exact kind of fight that once felt entirely foreign, armed with refined jiu-jitsu forged through years of humility and rigorous hard work. A Striker At Heart Pacio’s martial arts journey began in Baguio City, where an overweight 12-year-old originally discovered the art of wushu. Striking quickly became his first love, while grappling never stirred that same internal fire. Back then, it was merely a necessary box he was expected to tick. For years, sheer athleticism and quick instincts successfully carried him to the top. A sharp striking base coupled with functional takedown defense and a handful of submissions were all he required to capture gold. Yet, by his own admission, he never truly appreciated “the gentle art” until he co-founded Lions Nation MMA in 2023 and came under the meticulous wing of Gibran Langbayan, the very first Igorot jiu-jitsu black belt. Pacio told onefc.com: “While we were doing wushu, there was also jiu-jitsu, but we really didn’t focus much on it. When Professor Gibran came, I think that was the time that we became more enlightened on the true game of jiu-jitsu.” Photo credit: ONE Championship With two World Titles already permanently etched next to his name, Pacio could have easily settled for the exact formula that got him there. Instead, he fully embraced a white-belt mentality and rebuilt his ground training from the floor up. item.title: 5 players who hurt their 2027 PGA Tour prospects by missing Austin Championship cut
item.description: AUSTIN, Texas — There wasn’t much room for a bad week at the Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions, especially for players still trying to lock up their PGA Tour cards for 2027. The penultimate event of the 2026 FedEx Cup Fall brought 120 players to Omni Barton Creek Resort with plenty at stake, including a $1.08 million winner’s check and precious points in the race to finish inside the top 100. For some notable names, though, the week in Austin ended after just two rounds. The second round finished Saturday morning at Omni Barton Creek Resort's Fazio Canyons course, and these big names were sent packing. The cut line came in at 4 under par. Peter Malnati (3 under, started week 149 in FEC, now 151) Malnati made bogey on each of the first two holes of the tournament and never caught up. His second round was bogey-free, but with just two birdies, it wasn't enough to make the weekend. He's now just outside the number to get tiered conditional status. Davis Thompson (3 under, started week at 94, now 98) The stakes during the FedEx Cup Fall can get intense, and Thompson is a perfect example. He entered the week at No. 94, right on the edge of keeping full PGA Tour status, and needed only a par on his final hole Friday to make the cut. Instead, he knocked his approach into the water, made bogey and missed the weekend by a single shot. Now he has to hope one costly swing doesn’t ultimately cost him his card. Taylor Pendrith (2 under, started week at 104, now 107) The back nine at Fazio Canyons is significantly harder than the front and Pendrith started Thursday on the back by going three over in his first four holes. He fought to get back to the cutline, but couldn't make it. What looked like a golden opportunity to slip inside the top 100 has fallen away. Taylor Moore (1 under, started week at 92, now 97) After finishing third at Bermuda and putting himself in great position, Moore has missed two consecutive cuts now, at a tough time to do so. Moore's second round was tough at the beginning and the end: He opened with bogey on three of the first four holes and then closed with two more bogeys to fall on the wrong side of the cut. Chris Kirk (2 over, started week at 102, now 105) Much like with Pendrith, Austin seemed like a great spot for Kirk to climb into the top 100, but two consecutive over-par rounds have him going in the wrong direction. item.description: Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley starts his day before sunrise with a Shipley Do-Nuts cold brew, Dave Matthews Band and questions about how to improve Houston's early-down offense. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) It's about 4:30 a.m. Tuesday when Nick Caley walks out the door of his Missouri City home and hops into his car for work, running on less than five hours of sleep. On the 20-minute drive to Reliant Stadium, he stops at a Shipley Do-Nuts near his house and orders the same thing he always does: a caramel cold brew with light ice. He takes a sip, turns up the radio and listens to the sweet sounds of the Dave Matthews Band on Spotify as he ponders how he can help the Texans offense get better on early downs. The Texans are 3-5 for the second time in two seasons as they try to climb back into playoff contention. They travel to Cleveland this weekend - an hour from where Caley grew up - to face the Browns at noon on Sunday. The biggest difference between this season's 3-5 start and last year's is that Houston's offense, rather than its defense, is keeping the team afloat. The Texans rank third in the NFL in passing yards per game and 11th in points per game, far ahead of where they were a year ago. And this feels like the tip of the iceberg for this offense and its 43-year-old play-caller. Quarterback C.J. Stroud has thrived this season as the passing game unintentionally became the Texans' strength under Nick Caley after they made moves to improve the rushing attack in the offseason. item.title: Van Bommel: ‘Italy didn’t surprise me, maybe France underestimated them’
item.description: Van Bommel: ‘Italy didn’t surprise me, maybe France underestimated them’ Belgium coach Mark van Bommel says Italy’s 3-1 win over France didn’t surprise him, and he suggested Les Bleus may have underestimated Roberto Mancini’s side. With quotes via the Corriere dello Sport , the former Milan midfielder spoke at his pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday’s Nations League showdown with Italy in Brussels, which kicks off at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT] at the King Baudouin Stadium. Belgium must win to reach the quarter-finals. They’re third in Group A1 with nine points, one behind Italy and France. Italy will go through with a draw, and they’ll top the group if they win. “It’s an important game that would allow us to continue or not,” Van Bommel said. “It’s a test comparable to other cups, an interesting game to play under pressure. We always prepare the same way, whether it’s a final or not. “Tomorrow only victory counts, but it’s not a final that lets you win a cup.” ROME, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 25: Mark van Bommel head coach of Belgium celebrates after winning the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Italy and Belgium at Stadio Olimpico on September 25, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi/Getty Images) Van Bommel on Italy, France and Lukaku Italy go into the game full of confidence after beating France at San Siro on Thursday . Pio Esposito scored twice, and Zinedine Zidane suffered his first defeat as France coach. “Italy didn’t surprise me, and Turkey also deserved more against France,” Van Bommel continued. “Italy are a very good team. Maybe France took them lightly, but it doesn’t surprise me.” Belgium kept their hopes alive with a 2-1 comeback win in Turkey on Thursday, with Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere scoring. Van Bommel also confirmed Romelu Lukaku will have a role to play, whether from the start or off the bench. “He’s always important, whether he starts or comes on as a substitute. He’s a player with a lot of experience, and it’s a good thing to have him in a full stadium.”
